title: This robot picks 1,500 things an hour. Its maker is worth $1.45B.
caption:
Swipe to see the robot hand that has roboticists raving.

Eka Robotics raised a roughly $150 million Series A led by a16z and F-Prime, at a post-money valuation of $1.45 billion.

Co-founded by MIT professor Pulkit Agrawal and former Google DeepMind researcher Tuomas Haarnoja, Eka pairs a force-sensitive gripper with what it calls a vision-force-action model, trained with reinforcement learning in a physics simulator. The company says its robot picks about 1,500 objects an hour, versus about 600 for a person, and succeeds more than 95% of the time.

The gripper costs under $1,000, and Eka is running pilots with industrial customers on pick-and-place and wire-handling tasks. "They are already exceeding superhuman performance for certain tasks," said a16z general partner Raghu Raghuram, who co-led the round.
